items.informal_name: Product Rule for Hasse Derivatives in Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Product Rule for Partial Derivatives in Multivariate Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i : σ} {f g : MvPolynomial σ R},
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) (f * g) = (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) f * g + f * (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) g
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, and variables $ i \in \sigma $, the partial derivative with respect to $ i $ of the product of two multivariate polynomials $ f $ and $ g $ in $ R[\sigma] $ satisfies the Leibniz rule: $ \partial_i(fg) = (\partial_i f) \cdot g + f \cdot (\partial_i g) $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Generalized Product Rule for Polynomial Derivatives
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {ι : Type y} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] {s : Multiset ι} {f : ι → Polynomial R},
  Polynomial.derivative (Multiset.map f s).prod =
    (Multiset.map (fun i => (Multiset.map f (s.erase i)).prod * Polynomial.derivative (f i)) s).sum
items.informal_description:
For any commutative semiring $ R $, a multiset $ s $ of indices $ \iota $, and a function $ f: \iota \to R[X] $, the derivative of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $ satisfies:
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \left(\frac{d}{dx}f(i) \cdot \prod_{j \in s \setminus \{i\}} f(j)\right).
$$
This generalizes the product rule to the derivative of a product of multiple polynomials.

items.informal_name: Commutativity of Partial Derivatives with Evaluation in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {S : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) (f : τ → S) (j : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.aeval (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (⇑MvPolynomial.C ∘ f))) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl j)) p) =
    (MvPolynomial.pderiv j) ((MvPolynomial.aeval (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (⇑MvPolynomial.C ∘ f))) p)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ in variables $ \sigma \oplus \tau $ with coefficients in a commutative ring $ R $, and an $ R $-algebra homomorphism evaluating variables in $ \tau $ via a function $ f : \tau \to S $, the partial derivative of $ p $ with respect to $ j \in \sigma $ commutes with evaluation. Specifically, evaluating the partial derivative $ \partial_{\text{inl}(j)} p $ using the homomorphism that maps $ \sigma $-variables to themselves and $ \tau $-variables via $ f $ is equivalent to first evaluating $ p $ under this homomorphism and then taking the partial derivative with respect to $ j $. This establishes $ \text{aeval}(\partial_{\text{inl}(j)} p) = \partial_j(\text{aeval}(p)) $ in the target algebra $ S $.

items.name: Polynomial.hasseDeriv_coeff
items.type: {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ) : ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)

items.name: Polynomial.hasseDeriv_apply
items.type: {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) : (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)

items.name: Polynomial.hasseDeriv_monomial
items.type: {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R) : (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)

items.name: Polynomial.hasseDeriv_mul
items.type: {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R) : (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) = ∑ ij ∈ Finset.HasAntidiagonal.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Tensor Product Polynomial in Universal Factorization Context
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n m k : ℕ) (hn : n = m + k) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i))
      ((MvPolynomial.tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R)
        ((MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn) (MvPolynomial.X j))) =
    if ↑j < ↑i then 0
    else if h : ↑j - ↑i < k then MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr ⟨↑j - ↑i, h⟩) else if ↑j - ↑i = k then 1 else 0
items.informal_description: The partial derivative of the tensor-equivalent polynomial $ \text{tensorEquivSum}(R, \text{Fin} \, m, \text{Fin} \, k, R, \text{universalFactorizationMap}(R, n, m, k, h_n, X_j)) $ with respect to the variable $ \text{Sum.inl} \, i $ yields: $ 0 $ if $ j < i $; $ X_{\text{inr}(j - i)} $ if $ j - i < k $; $ 1 $ if $ j - i = k $; and $ 0 $ otherwise. This describes how differentiation interacts with tensor product structures in multivariate polynomial rings under universal factorization maps.

This describes how the partial derivative acts on the embedded variable in the tensor product structure of multivariate polynomial rings.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),

items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Generalized Product Rule for Polynomial Derivatives
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {ι : Type y} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] {s : Multiset ι} {f : ι → Polynomial R},
  Polynomial.derivative (Multiset.map f s).prod =
    (Multiset.map (fun i => (Multiset.map f (s.erase i)).prod * Polynomial.derivative (f i)) s).sum
items.informal_description:
For any commutative semiring $ R $, a multiset $ s $ of indices $ \iota $, and a function $ f: \iota \to R[X] $, the derivative of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $ satisfies:
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right) = \sum_{i \in s} \left(\frac{d}{dx}f(i) \cdot \prod_{j \in s \setminus \{i\}} f(j)\right).
$$
This generalizes the product rule to the derivative of a product of multiple polynomials.
